definitionEn: An animal with hair that feeds its babies on milk.
example: Dolphins are mammals, so they breathe air through their lungs.

definitionEn: A cold-blooded animal with scaly skin, such as a snake or lizard.
example: Snakes and lizards are reptiles that rely on the sun for warmth.

definitionEn: A small animal with six legs and a body divided into three parts.
example: Bees are important insects because they help plants produce fruit.

definitionEn: A group of living things that can breed with each other.
example: Scientists have discovered hundreds of new species in the rainforest this year.

definitionEn: An animal kept at home for company and pleasure.
example: Many families keep a pet, such as a cat or a dog.

definitionEn: The thick hair that covers the body of many animals.
example: The rabbit's soft fur turned white during the winter months.

definitionEn: A sharp, curved nail on the foot of an animal.
example: The cat scratched my hand with its sharp claws.

definitionEn: To chase and kill animals for food or sport.
example: Lions hunt zebras on the open plains at dusk.

definitionEn: A large group of one kind of animal that lives or moves together.
example: A herd of elephants crossed the river slowly in the morning.

definitionEn: A structure built by birds or some animals to lay eggs in.
example: A blackbird built its nest in the hedge behind our house.

definitionEn: One of the light, soft growths that cover a bird's body.
example: The peacock's bright feathers are used to attract a mate.

definitionEn: The part at the back of an animal's body that sticks out.
example: The monkey wrapped its long tail around a branch to stay steady.

definitionEn: To eat grass that is growing in a field.
example: Sheep graze quietly on the hillside throughout the afternoon.

definitionEn: A group of wild animals, such as wolves, that hunt together.
example: A pack of wolves followed the herd for several miles across the snow.

definitionEn: A large group of insects or small animals moving together.
example: A swarm of bees settled on the branch near our kitchen window.

definitionEn: A box or structure where honeybees live and make honey.
example: The beekeeper opened the hive to check on the queen bee.

definitionEn: Trained to live with people and not be wild or fearful.
example: The fox became tame after weeks of being fed by the farmer.

definitionEn: A flat, thin part of a fish's body used for swimming.
example: The shark's dorsal fin cut through the surface of the water.

definitionEn: An animal that eats only plants and plant material.
example: Cows are herbivores, feeding mainly on grass and hay all day.

definitionEn: An animal that eats mainly or only the flesh of other animals.
example: Lions are carnivores that hunt antelope and other large mammals on the savanna.

definitionEn: An animal that eats both plants and other animals.
example: Pigs are omnivores, so they will eat roots, fruit, and even insects.

definitionEn: To spend the winter in a deep sleep to save energy.
example: Bears hibernate through the cold winter months without eating or drinking.

definitionEn: A hole or tunnel dug in the ground by an animal to live in.
example: The rabbits escaped into their burrow when the fox approached the field.

meaningVi: kiếm ăn, lục tìm thức ăn
definitionEn: To search widely for food, especially for animals.
example: Deer forage for leaves and berries along the forest edge at dawn.

definitionEn: An animal that feeds on dead animals or waste it finds.
example: Vultures are scavengers that feed on carcasses left behind by predators.

definitionEn: An area that an animal defends as its own for food or mating.
example: The male lion patrols his territory to warn rivals to stay away.

definitionEn: A natural tendency or ability that an animal is born with.
example: Sea turtles follow an instinct that guides them back to the beach where they hatched.

definitionEn: A poison that some snakes, spiders, or insects inject into their prey.
example: The cobra injected enough venom into the mouse to paralyse it instantly.

definitionEn: Having a poison that can be injected through a bite or sting.
example: Many people wrongly fear that every snake in the forest is venomous.

definitionEn: A mammal, such as a kangaroo, that carries its young in a pouch.
example: Koalas are marsupials, and the babies stay in the mother's pouch for months.

definitionEn: A mammal of the group that includes monkeys, apes, and humans.
example: Chimpanzees are primates that use simple tools to find food.

definitionEn: A small mammal with large front teeth, such as a mouse or rat.
example: Squirrels and beavers are rodents that gnaw through wood with their teeth.

definitionEn: An animal that lives both on land and in water, such as a frog.
example: Frogs and toads are amphibians that lay their eggs in fresh water.

definitionEn: Living or growing in or on water.
example: Hippos spend most of the day in aquatic environments to keep cool.

definitionEn: The feathers covering a bird's body, especially their colour and pattern.
example: The male peacock displays its brilliant plumage to attract a partner.

definitionEn: To come together to produce young, as animals do.
example: Male seahorses mate with females, but the males carry the eggs.

definitionEn: To shed old feathers, fur, or skin so that new growth can appear.
example: Snakes moult their skin several times as they grow larger each year.

definitionEn: To rest or sleep perched on a branch or ledge, as birds do.
example: Pigeons roost on the high ledges of old buildings in the city centre.

meaningVi: hệ thống phân loại sinh vật
definitionEn: The science of classifying living organisms into groups based on shared characteristics.
example: Modern taxonomy relies heavily on genetic analysis to group related species together.

definitionEn: The mental processes of perceiving, learning, remembering and reasoning.
example: Researchers study animal cognition to understand how crows solve complex puzzles.

definitionEn: Relating to the scientific study of animals and their behaviour.
example: The zoological garden opened a new enclosure for its rare Asian elephants.

definitionEn: The study of the form and structure of organisms and their parts.
example: The morphology of the bat's wing allowed it to fly through dense forest.

definitionEn: A close, long-term relationship in which two different species live together and benefit.
example: The relationship between clownfish and sea anemones is a classic example of symbiosis.

meaningVi: ký sinh trùng, sinh vật ký sinh
definitionEn: An organism that lives on or in another organism and harms it.
example: Ticks are parasites that feed on the blood of mammals and birds.

definitionEn: Living on or in another organism and feeding on it.
example: The cuckoo is parasitic because it lays its eggs in other birds' nests.

definitionEn: The act of an animal hunting and killing other animals for food.
example: Heavy predation by foxes has reduced the local rabbit population considerably.

definitionEn: Defending a particular area against other animals of the same species.
example: Male robins are highly territorial and will chase intruders from their gardens.

definitionEn: The regular seasonal movement of animals from one region to another.
example: The annual migration of wildebeest across the Serengeti attracts thousands of tourists.

definitionEn: An animal that has a backbone, including fish, birds, reptiles and mammals.
example: Fish, frogs, and humans are all vertebrates with a spinal column.

definitionEn: An animal without a backbone, such as an insect, worm, or snail.
example: Most invertebrates, such as crabs and octopuses, live in the ocean.

definitionEn: Living in trees or spending most of its time in them.
example: Many lemurs are arboreal, leaping between branches with remarkable agility.

definitionEn: Living in groups or enjoying the company of others, especially animals.
example: Flamingos are gregarious birds that gather in flocks of several thousand.

definitionEn: Preferring to live or spend time alone rather than in a group.
example: Tigers are largely solitary animals that hunt and rest on their own.

meaningVi: du mục, di chuyển liên tục
definitionEn: Moving from place to place in search of food or water, rather than settling.
example: Some nomadic species follow the rains across the steppe in search of fresh grass.

definitionEn: A hoofed mammal, such as a horse, deer, or cow.
example: Giraffes and zebras are ungulates that survive by grazing on open grassland.

definitionEn: An animal that walks on four legs.
example: Most mammals are quadrupeds, but humans walk upright on only two legs.

definitionEn: Walking on two legs rather than four.
example: Ostriches are bipedal, running swiftly across the desert on their long legs.

definitionEn: The animal life of a particular region, habitat, or geological period.
example: The island's unique fauna includes several species of birds found nowhere else.

definitionEn: A large natural region defined by its climate, plants, and animals.
example: The tundra is a cold biome where few animals can survive the winter.

definitionEn: Relating to the relationships between organisms and their environment.
example: The ecological role of beavers includes creating wetlands that many species depend on.

definitionEn: A group of closely related species in biological classification.
example: Scientists placed the newly found frog in a different genus.

definitionEn: A system in which members of a group are ranked by importance or status.
example: Wolves maintain a strict social hierarchy within each pack.

meaningVi: tiếng kêu, tiếng phát ra của động vật
definitionEn: A sound, call, or cry made by an animal to communicate.
example: Whale vocalisations can travel hundreds of kilometres through deep ocean water.

definitionEn: A method of finding objects by sending out sounds and listening for echoes.
example: Bats use echolocation to catch moths in complete darkness.

meaningVi: trạng thái ngừng hoạt động tạm thời
definitionEn: A state of inactivity in which growth or movement is temporarily suspended.
example: Some desert toads enter dormancy during long dry periods and wait for rain.

definitionEn: The period of pregnancy from conception to birth in mammals.
example: Elephants have one of the longest gestation periods of any land animal.

definitionEn: The ability to produce a large number of offspring.
example: Rats have high fecundity, so their populations can grow very rapidly.

definitionEn: The movement of animals or seeds away from their place of origin.
example: Young wolves undergo dispersal, leaving the pack to find new territory.

definitionEn: Active during the day rather than at night.
example: Squirrels are diurnal, spending their daylight hours gathering nuts and seeds.

definitionEn: The highest point, or the top predator in a food chain.
example: Sharks are an apex predator, sitting at the very top of the marine food chain.

definitionEn: A species whose presence affects its ecosystem far more than its numbers suggest.
example: Sea otters are a keystone species because they keep sea urchin numbers under control.

definitionEn: Relating to mammals, which feed their young with milk and have hair.
example: Mammalian brains share many structures that were present in early ancestors.

definitionEn: Relating to birds or the bird group of animals.
example: Avian species often show remarkable navigation skills during long seasonal flights.

meaningVi: ngủ hè (trạng thái ngủ qua mùa khô)
definitionEn: To pass the summer or a dry season in a dormant, inactive state.
example: Some desert snails aestivate under rocks until the first summer rains arrive.

meaningVi: sống ở biển, di cư ngược về sông đẻ trứng
definitionEn: Describing fish that migrate from the sea into fresh water to spawn.
example: Atlantic salmon are anadromous, returning to the rivers where they were born.

meaningVi: sống ở nước ngọt, ra biển đẻ trứng
definitionEn: Describing fish that live in fresh water but migrate to the sea to spawn.
example: European eels are catadromous, travelling great distances to the ocean to breed.

meaningVi: hội sinh (một bên hưởng lợi, bên kia không hại)
definitionEn: Describing a relationship where one species benefits while the other is neither helped nor harmed.
example: Barnacles living on whales form a commensal relationship that costs the whale little.

definitionEn: Describing an animal that feeds mainly on fish.
example: Kingfishers are piscivorous birds that dive headfirst into rivers to catch prey.

definitionEn: Describing an animal that mainly eats insects.
example: Many bats are insectivorous, consuming thousands of moths and beetles each night.

definitionEn: Describing an animal whose diet consists mainly of fruit.
example: Many tropical birds are frugivorous and help scatter seeds across the forest.

definitionEn: Describing an animal that feeds mainly on seeds and grains.
example: Finches are granivorous birds, cracking open seeds with their strong beaks.

definitionEn: Permanently attached to one place and unable to move, like barnacles or corals.
example: Adult barnacles are sessile, cementing themselves to rocks and ship hulls.

definitionEn: A marine mollusc, such as an octopus or squid, with tentacles around its head.
example: Cuttlefish are remarkable cephalopods capable of changing colour within seconds.

definitionEn: A mollusc, such as a snail or slug, that moves on a single muscular foot.
example: Land gastropods lose moisture quickly, so they prefer damp and shady places.

definitionEn: An aquatic animal with a hard shell and jointed legs, such as a crab or shrimp.
example: Lobsters and crabs are crustaceans that moult their shells as they grow.

definitionEn: An eight-legged creature with two body segments, such as a spider or scorpion.
example: Scientists have identified more than fifty thousand species of arachnid worldwide.

definitionEn: A reptile of the group that includes turtles and tortoises, with a bony shell.
example: The chelonian shell is fused to the ribs, forming a protective armour.

meaningVi: hoạt động lúc bình minh và hoàng hôn
definitionEn: Active mainly at dawn and dusk, during twilight.
example: Rabbits are crepuscular, feeding most actively in the early morning and evening.

definitionEn: Capable of flying, or relating to flight in animals.
example: Bats are the only mammals that are truly volant, using wings to fly.

meaningVi: sự bắt chước về hình dạng, màu sắc
definitionEn: The resemblance of one species to another, which offers protection from predators.
example: Hoverflies display mimicry, looking very much like stinging wasps and bees.

definitionEn: Describing bright colours that warn predators that an animal is poisonous.
example: The poison dart frog's aposematic colouring signals danger to would-be predators.

definitionEn: Designed to be hidden or hard to notice, especially through colour or shape.
example: The stick insect's cryptic body makes it almost invisible against bark.

meaningVi: lưỡng hình (đực cái khác nhau rõ)
definitionEn: Describing a species in which males and females look markedly different.

definitionEn: Describing an animal that mates with several partners during one breeding season.
example: Male red deer are polygamous, gathering harems of several females each autumn.

meaningVi: một vợ một chồng, gắn bó một bạn đời
definitionEn: Describing an animal that forms a lasting pair bond with one partner.
example: Many species of gibbon are monogamous, with pairs staying together for life.

meaningVi: xu hướng gắn bó với nơi sinh
definitionEn: The tendency of an animal to remain in or return to its birthplace.

definitionEn: Describing an animal that reproduces by laying eggs that hatch outside the body.
example: Most birds and reptiles are oviparous, depositing eggs in nests or sand.

definitionEn: Describing an animal that gives birth to live young rather than laying eggs.
example: Most mammals are viviparous, nourishing their embryos internally until birth.

definitionEn: Relating to lizards or a lizard-like reptile.
example: The saurian tail can regenerate after being lost to a predator.

definitionEn: Relating to snakes or their characteristics.

definitionEn: A hoofed animal, such as a cow or sheep, that chews the cud.

definitionEn: Adapted for running, as in animals with long legs built for speed.

definitionEn: Adapted for digging and living underground, as in moles and badgers.

meaningVi: trạng thái lờ đờ, hạ nhiệt tạm thời
definitionEn: A state of reduced activity and body temperature, lasting for a short period.
example: Hummingbirds enter torpor at night to conserve energy when food is scarce.

meaningVi: lây từ động vật sang người

definitionEn: Relying on external sources of heat to regulate body temperature.

definitionEn: Generating body heat internally to maintain a stable temperature.

definitionEn: Relating to fish or resembling a fish.

definitionEn: Relating to wolves or resembling a wolf.

definitionEn: Relating to bears or resembling a bear.

definitionEn: Relating to foxes, or cunning and sly in manner.

definitionEn: Relating to pigs or resembling a pig.
example: The farmer noted the porcine look of the young boars in the enclosure.

definitionEn: Relating to cattle, or slow and dull in manner.

definitionEn: Relating to horses, donkeys, or other members of the horse family.

definitionEn: An insect of the order that includes butterflies and moths.

definitionEn: Describing an organism that feeds on dead organic matter, such as decaying leaves.

definitionEn: The branch of zoology concerned with the study of fish.
